Trestle Freight proposes a $188,000 base salary and an $18,000 signing bonus for a June 1 start. The role would give Mara ownership of the internal security platform and responsibility for preparing it for the July audit.

For the first 12 weeks, we can schedule two three-day site visits per month, with Trestle covering travel expenses. We can also limit Mara’s incident coverage to business hours, with a designated partner handling after-hours escalation and Mara training that partner as part of onboarding.

Can Mara commit to June 1 and that visit schedule? If June 1 is tight, what is her earliest firm start date? We can discuss how the signing bonus would change with a later start and how much time she’d need before the audit.

Mara can commit to June 1 and two three-day site visits per month for the first 12 weeks if we agree on the written package. The $188,000 base and $18,000 signing bonus work for June 1, provided the bonus is paid with her first paycheck and at least $12,000 is protected from repayment if Trestle ends her employment without cause. That portion covers equity she would give up by starting before June 15. July 1 is her earliest firm alternative if we can’t agree on the June terms.

We’d propose remote work between visits, with Trestle covering travel and lodging, and up to two grouped visits per month after onboarding, scheduled by mutual agreement. Please confirm that platform ownership includes authority over security architecture and technical priorities. The offer should also specify business-hours incident coverage, with a named primary and backup for after-hours escalation in place at the start. Mara can train them during onboarding.

For the July audit, Mara can lead platform readiness from June 1. Before we recommend acceptance, we need to confirm the audit date and scope, any known gaps, and who will provide access, evidence, and remediation support. What’s the audit date, and who owns those dependencies today?

Trestle can put a June 1 start, a $188,000 base salary, and an $18,000 signing bonus in the written offer. We’ll pay the bonus with Mara’s first paycheck, and the full $18,000 will be protected from repayment if Trestle ends her employment without cause.

Mara will own the internal security platform, including decision-making authority over its security architecture and technical priorities. She’ll work remotely between two three-day site visits per month during the first 12 weeks. After that, any site visits will be grouped, capped at two per month, and scheduled by mutual agreement. Trestle will cover travel and lodging for those visits.

Mara’s incident coverage will be limited to business hours. Trestle will name a primary and backup for after-hours escalation before June 1, and Mara will train both during onboarding.

Mara will lead platform readiness for the July audit from June 1. I don’t have a confirmed audit date or the current dependency owners to share yet. Before asking you to recommend acceptance, I’ll confirm the audit date and scope, document the known gaps, and identify who will provision access, supply evidence, and support remediation. I’ll include those details and the names of the escalation contacts in the written package.

The June 1 package works for Mara on compensation, architecture authority, travel, and incident coverage as described. The outstanding dependency is whether the audit timeline is feasible once the scope, known gaps, and support commitments are clear.

Please include the dates Mara can expect platform access and evidence, and name the Trestle sponsor who can resolve delays or assign remediation resources. We propose that Mara lead platform readiness and flag risks, with that sponsor accountable for resolving cross-team blockers and deciding how to handle any gaps that remain at the audit deadline. With those responsibilities and the after-hours contacts in writing, we can assess the timeline and make our recommendation.

We can write the audit responsibilities that way. Mara will lead platform readiness from June 1 and flag risks to the audit timeline. Trestle’s named sponsor will be accountable for resolving cross-team blockers, assigning remediation resources, and deciding how to handle gaps still open at the audit deadline.

The June 1 package will include a written audit plan with the confirmed audit date and scope, known gaps, the dates Mara can expect platform access and evidence, and the named owners responsible for delivering them. It will also name the sponsor, document the remediation support Trestle is committing, and identify the primary and backup for after-hours escalation.

The dates and names are still pending confirmation. We’ll send the completed package for your feasibility review before asking you to recommend acceptance.

Ivo proposes a fixed fee of **$42,750 for a guaranteed 50-day design engagement**. That’s a 5% discount on the standard $900 day rate. To secure the block and the discount, Hearth would sign the agreement and pay a 30% deposit of $12,825 within three business days of signing. The reservation takes effect when the deposit arrives.

The fee covers concept design, design development, and a final design package for the fabricator. At kickoff, we’d agree on accessibility requirements, venue and transport constraints, and the drawings and specifications the fabricator needs. Hearth would provide one consolidated round of feedback at concept review and one at design development. Additional revisions or scope changes would require written approval at $900 per day.

The remaining payments would be $17,100 on delivery of the design development package and $12,825 on delivery of the final package, each due within 15 days. Fabrication supervision would be a separate engagement at $900 per day, with dates agreed before booking. Ivo would have permission to show cleared exhibit photographs in their portfolio and presentations after the public opening.

What is the fabrication slot deadline, when does the fabricator need the final drawings, and can Hearth commit to the full block and deposit on that timetable? If procurement needs more time for the deposit, Ivo can discuss a shorter initial booking at the standard rate.

Hearth can guarantee 46 days at Ivo’s standard $900 day rate, for a fixed fee of **$41,400**, including two on-site installation days. The payment schedule would be **$8,280 (20%) within three business days of signing**, then **$8,280 at concept delivery, $12,420 at design development delivery, and $12,420 at final package delivery**, each milestone payment due within 15 days. Can Ivo reserve the block on signature, with the deposit due on that timetable?

The fee would cover concept design, design development, an accessible alternate layout, and a fabrication-ready package with editable native files, drawings, and specifications. At kickoff we’d agree on accessibility criteria for both layouts, venue and transport constraints, and the fabricator’s file requirements. Hearth can consolidate feedback into one round at concept and one at design development. Additional revisions, scope changes, or fabrication supervision beyond the two installation days would require written approval at $900 per day. If site travel is the sticking point, we can discuss a separate, pre-agreed travel allowance.

I don’t have confirmed dates to give you for the fabrication reservation cutoff or final drawing handoff. We can put both dates in the agreement before signing and work backward to set kickoff, review dates, and the two installation days. What’s Ivo’s earliest available kickoff, and how much lead time does Ivo need from kickoff to final handoff, including Hearth’s review periods?

Ivo would retain copyright. Once the fee is paid, Hearth would have a perpetual, royalty-free license to use and adapt the design and editable files for fabrication, installation, touring, and future presentations of this exhibit, including sharing them with its fabricators and venues for that work. Ivo could use cleared photos in portfolios and presentations once the touring venue opens, scheduled for two months after launch. Could Ivo agree to those terms?

Ivo can reserve the 46-day block on signature at **$41,400**, with the **$8,280 deposit due within three business days**. If the deposit is late, Ivo may release the dates after written notice. The proposed concept, design development, and final payments work on the amounts and 15-day terms Hearth set out.

Ivo can allocate 44 days to design and two to on-site installation support. The design fee covers both layouts, the fabrication-ready drawings and specifications, editable native files, and the two consolidated revision rounds. Let’s set the installation dates and a separate travel allowance before signing. Hearth’s fabricator would supervise the installation. Any fabrication supervision requested from Ivo would need advance dates and written approval at $900 per day.

Ivo proposes kickoff on the first business day after the deposit clears, subject to confirming the calendar before signature. Please allow **11 weeks from kickoff to final handoff**, including two review periods of up to five business days each. Once Hearth has the fabrication reservation cutoff and drawing deadline, we can work backward and put specific dates in the agreement.

Ivo accepts the copyright and exhibit-specific license terms as proposed, including adaptation and file sharing with Hearth’s fabricators and venues. For photographs, could we tie permission to **each venue’s public opening**? Ivo could show cleared launch photographs in portfolios and presentations from launch day, and cleared photographs of the touring installation once that venue opens.

The sponsor embargo covers launch photographs as well as touring photographs. Ivo can use cleared photos from either installation in portfolios and presentations once the first touring venue opens to the public, currently scheduled for two months after launch. The actual opening date would control. Hearth can review Ivo’s proposed images in advance so the cleared set is ready when the embargo lifts.

Hearth agrees to 44 design days and two on-site installation support days within the $41,400 fee, with Hearth’s fabricator supervising installation. We propose reimbursing reasonable, documented travel expenses for the two site days up to a cap agreed before signing. Please send an estimate so we can set that cap. We also accept release of the reserved dates after written notice if the deposit is overdue.

We’ll use the first business day after the deposit clears for kickoff and budget 11 weeks to final handoff, including both five-business-day review windows. The fabrication reservation cutoff and drawing deadline still need confirmation. We’ll use those dates to set the signing deadline and confirm kickoff, both reviews, final handoff, and the installation dates before signing. If the fabricator needs information sooner to hold the slot, could Ivo issue an early package limited to what the fabricator needs for the reservation, within the 44 design days?

Ivo can include an early reservation package within the 44 design days and the $41,400 fee. Please send the fabricator’s minimum requirements and cutoff as soon as they’re confirmed. Before signing, we can agree on the contents and delivery date and check that they fit the 11-week schedule. Ivo would mark the package “preliminary — for slot reservation only.” The final handoff would supply the drawings authorized for fabrication.

For budgeting, Ivo proposes a **provisional travel cap of $1,500** for one trip covering two consecutive site days. That assumes $600 for round-trip transport, $500 for two nights’ lodging, and $400 for local transit and meals. Hearth would reimburse actual, documented expenses up to the agreed cap. Please send the installation location and proposed dates so Ivo can check fares and lodging before we fix the cap.

Ivo accepts the sponsor embargo. Ivo may use cleared photographs from either installation in portfolios and presentations starting on the actual public opening date of the first touring venue. Advance image review works for Ivo.

Hearth can budget for the provisional $1,500 travel cap for one trip covering two consecutive installation days, with reimbursement for actual, documented expenses. We’ll send the installation location and proposed dates for Ivo to check before we fix the cap in the agreement.

The early reservation package can be marked “preliminary — for slot reservation only,” with the final handoff supplying the drawings authorized for fabrication. The fabricator’s minimum requirements, reservation cutoff, and final drawing deadline are still pending. Once we have them, we’ll confirm the early package contents and due date with Ivo and check that the 11-week schedule fits before signing.

We propose that Dev start as director-designate by September 1 at a $138,000 annual salary rate. We would seek board approval for the January appointment before the overlap begins, so Dev can rely on a January 1 start as director at $155,000 annually. The incumbent would remain director through December 31.

During the overlap, we propose giving Dev procurement authority up to $60,000 per purchase, effective when the board approves the delegation. The board would retain personnel decisions through December 31. Dev would lead the operating plan and budget handoff. The incumbent would remain accountable for operations, introduce Dev to key partners, and document open commitments. We propose a joint handoff review in December so both boards can see who owns each outstanding item in January.

What on-site schedule could Dev commit to during the overlap, and would Dev need to relocate for January? We can offer up to $8,000 total for temporary lodging, training, or a mix of the two. We’d like to settle the on-site dates and how to allocate that support before either board considers the plan.

Dev can commit to two on-site blocks each month before relocating after the school term in December. For the next September 1 start, we propose the following 2027 dates, with Dev working remotely between blocks.

| Month | First on-site block | Second on-site block |
|---|---|---|
| September | 1–3 | 13–17 |
| October | 4–8 | 18–22 |
| November | 1–5 | 15–19 |
| December | 6–10 | 13–17 |

Dev can accept the $138,000 annual rate during the overlap if Caldera reserves the full $8,000 for lodging and books or reimburses the agreed blocks. If the quotes come in under budget, we can agree together to use the balance for training. Dev would relocate in time to serve locally from January 1, 2028.

Before Dev starts, we’d need a signed agreement and a board resolution approving the January 1 appointment at $155,000, effective automatically on that date. We propose holding the joint handoff review on December 16 and naming an owner and deadline for each open commitment. Unfinished items would carry forward on that list without delaying the appointment.

The proposed $60,000 per-purchase limit works if the delegation takes effect September 1. Through December 31, the incumbent would own outage decisions and after-hours escalation, including during Dev’s on-site blocks. From January 1, Dev would own outage response and have written authority to direct crews, call in staff and contractors, and authorize emergency work within the limit. For spending above it, Caldera would name an approver and backup reachable around the clock. The board could retain formal personnel decisions during the overlap while leaving incident staffing clear.

If Caldera delays the title or operating authority beyond January 1, the $155,000 rate would still take effect that day. The board would name the acting director accountable for outages until Dev receives the authority. If the transfer is still incomplete January 31, Dev could elect a written extension with a new firm date or leave with eight weeks’ base pay. Can Caldera take that fallback and the emergency delegation to its board alongside the appointment?

Yes. Caldera will take the emergency delegation and the January fallback to its board alongside the appointment. The eight weeks’ separation pay requires express board approval. We’ll seek a vote on the full package and, if approved, provide Dev with the resolution and a signed agreement before September 1, 2027.

- **Appointment and pay.** Dev starts as director-designate on September 1 at a $138,000 annual rate. The incumbent remains director through December 31. The resolution appoints Dev director effective January 1, 2028, at $155,000 annually, without a second vote.
- **On-site work and relocation.** Caldera accepts all eight proposed blocks, with remote work between them. We’ll reserve $8,000 for lodging and offer to book the rooms directly so Dev can confirm the arrangements before starting. Caldera and Dev may jointly allocate any remaining balance to training once the rooms are booked. Dev will arrange the December move and serve locally from January 1.
- **Operating authority.** Dev’s $60,000 per-purchase procurement delegation takes effect September 1. Through December 31, the board retains personnel decisions, and the incumbent directs outage response and handles after-hours escalation, including when Dev is on site. From January 1, Dev has written authority to direct crews, call in staff and contractors, and authorize emergency work up to $60,000 per purchase. Before the transfer, Caldera will give Dev and the crews the names and 24-hour contact details of the primary approver and backup for spending above that limit.
- **Handoff.** Dev leads the operating plan and budget handoff. The incumbent introduces Dev to key partners and documents open commitments. At the December 16 review, Dev and the incumbent will assign each outstanding item an owner and deadline. Those items carry forward without delaying the appointment.
- **Delayed transfer.** If Caldera delays either the title or the agreed operating authority, Dev’s $155,000 rate still takes effect January 1. The board will identify an acting director and tell crews who is accountable for outages until Dev has the authority to take over. If either part of the transfer remains outstanding on January 31, Dev may elect a written extension with a new firm transfer date or leave with eight weeks’ base pay calculated at the $155,000 annual rate.

Noor proposes a fractional appointment to establish and lead Finch’s methods desk, starting at three days a week and moving to four in March. We’d put the step-up in the appointment letter now, with pay prorated from a $125,000 full-time annual salary. We’re flexible on title and would welcome a review after the first month at four days to assess workload and staffing.

Noor’s existing editorial project will continue independently for its remaining nine months, with its data and unfinished articles staying with the project. We can agree on a disclosure and recusal process for overlapping coverage, with a designated Finch editor handling matters from which Noor recuses.

Noor would have final say on methods corrections where Noor is unconflicted. Finch would retain its usual authority over publication and legal review. Would that division of authority work for Finch, and what staffing can Finch commit to at launch?

Finch can commit a deputy to cover the fourth submission day from the first week of December through February. We’d write Noor’s three-day schedule and the March increase to four days into the appointment letter, with a workload and staffing review after the first month at four days. We can meet the proposed $125,000 full-time rate, prorated to $75,000 annualized at three days and $100,000 at four, if Noor takes responsibility for training the deputy within Noor’s scheduled days.

Before launch, Noor and the deputy would document how to log and triage submissions, which decisions the deputy can make, and when to escalate to the duty editor. The deputy would hand off open items in writing. Urgent matters on the fourth day would go to the duty editor so coverage works without requiring Noor to be on call.

We propose that Noor lead the technical assessment of corrections and clear routine, uncontested changes. If an editor disputes a correction, Noor and the editor would record the point of disagreement and supporting evidence. The editor-in-chief would decide promptly whether and how Finch publishes the correction and record the rationale. The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority, and Finch’s usual legal review applies.

The existing project can continue independently for its remaining nine months. Its data and unfinished articles would stay with the project, and both teams would keep their working materials separate. Noor would disclose overlapping coverage at intake or as soon as it becomes apparent. A designated Finch editor would then handle the matter, including any subsequent correction.

Would Noor accept the training responsibility at that rate and the editor-in-chief’s role in resolving disputed corrections?

Noor accepts responsibility for training the deputy within the three scheduled days at the proposed rate. The coverage and handoff plan works for us, including routing urgent matters to the duty editor when Noor is off. Let’s put the automatic move to four days in March and the review after the first month at four days in the appointment letter. We also accept the proposed terms for the independent project and the recusal process.

For disputed corrections, we can agree to a written record of the disagreement and a prompt decision by the editor-in-chief on whether and when to publish, subject to Finch’s usual legal review. Noor needs final say on the technical finding and on whether the published wording accurately reflects it in cases where Noor is unconflicted. If the editor-in-chief decides to withhold or defer publication, the rationale can go in the record alongside Noor’s finding. Can Finch agree to that division of authority?

Finch can agree that Noor has final say on the methods desk’s technical finding in any case where Noor is unconflicted. Noor would review proposed correction wording for accuracy. Only wording Noor approves could be presented as the desk’s finding or attributed to Noor.

If the wording remains disputed, the editor-in-chief could defer or withhold publication, or publish a correction in Finch’s own editorial voice. If Finch publishes, it would accurately describe any desk finding it cites and make clear where its judgment differs. The record would include Noor’s finding, the disputed wording, and the editor-in-chief’s decision and rationale. The editor-in-chief would retain final authority over Finch’s wording and whether and when to publish, subject to the usual legal review.

Would that attribution safeguard work for Noor? We’ll include the agreed schedule, pay, deputy coverage and training, workload review, and outside-project terms in the appointment letter.

Yes. Noor accepts that division of authority. Noor has final say on the desk’s technical finding in unconflicted cases, and only wording Noor approves may be presented as the desk’s finding or attributed to Noor. Finch may publish in its own editorial voice, and any reference to the desk’s finding must accurately describe it and clearly distinguish Finch’s judgment. The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority, subject to usual legal review, with disputed corrections documented as proposed.

Please include those terms in the appointment letter alongside the agreed schedule, automatic March increase and corresponding pay, deputy coverage and training, workload review, and independent-project and recusal provisions.

**Finch Review | Letter of appointment**

Dear Noor,

Finch Review offers you the appointment of Methods Desk Editor to establish and lead the desk. The desk will begin accepting submissions four days a week in the first week of December 2026.

**Schedule and compensation.** From launch through February 2027, you will work three days a week at an annualized salary of $75,000. Beginning March 1, 2027, your schedule will automatically increase to four days a week and your annualized salary to $100,000. Both amounts are prorated from a full-time annual salary of $125,000. After your first month at four days, you and the editor-in-chief will review workload and staffing.

**Deputy coverage and training.** Finch will assign a deputy to cover the fourth submission day each week from launch through February. You will train the deputy within your three scheduled days. Before launch, you and the deputy will document how to log and triage submissions, which decisions the deputy can make, and when to escalate a matter to the duty editor. The deputy will hand off open items in writing and route urgent matters to the duty editor whenever you are off duty. You have no on-call obligation on those days.

**Findings and corrections.** In cases where you are unconflicted, you have final say on the desk’s technical finding and may clear routine, uncontested methods corrections. You will review proposed correction wording for accuracy. Only wording you approve may be presented as the desk’s finding or attributed to you.

If a correction is disputed, you and the editor involved will record your finding, the disputed wording, the point of disagreement, and the supporting evidence. The editor-in-chief will decide promptly whether and when to publish and will record the decision and rationale, including any reason for deferring or withholding publication. Finch may publish a correction in its own editorial voice. Any reference to the desk’s finding must describe it accurately and distinguish Finch’s judgment wherever it differs. The editor-in-chief retains final authority over Finch’s wording and publication, subject to Finch’s usual legal review and the attribution terms above.

**Independent project and recusal.** You may continue directing your existing editorial project independently for its remaining nine months. Its data and unfinished articles will stay with the project, and Finch and the project will keep their working materials separate. You will disclose overlapping coverage at intake or as soon as it becomes apparent and recuse yourself from the Finch matter. A designated Finch editor will handle it from that point, including any subsequent correction.
The appointment letter reflects our agreement. On Noor’s behalf, I accept Finch Review’s offer of appointment as Methods Desk Editor on the terms set out in the letter.

We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording.

**Use and access.** The Testing House may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare for, conduct and report the agreed actuator vibration tests. Only test personnel named in a list approved in writing by both parties may access the drawings, geometry or extracts. Each person must first be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The parties may approve additions or substitutions by email. Adviser or subcontractor status alone confers no access. The Testing House is responsible for each approved person’s compliance.

**Working copies and fixtures.** The Testing House may make the minimum working copies reasonably needed for the tests, with encryption in storage and in transit. It may extract the minimum geometry needed to design and fabricate fixtures solely for those tests. The same access and use limits apply to fixture files and physical fixtures. The Testing House must not reuse or disclose the drawings, geometry, extracts or fixtures to develop a competing product. It may retain test results and reports that do not disclose or permit reconstruction of the CAD geometry.

**Destruction and verification.** Within 30 days after the Design Owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the test work, the Testing House must securely erase the supplied files, working copies and derivative fixture files, and destroy physical fixtures made from the geometry. By the same deadline, it must provide a certificate from an independent verifier identifying the materials destroyed, the dates and methods of destruction, and any outstanding exceptions. The verifier may inspect records without receiving the CAD geometry. This certification replaces on-demand site access.

Can your backup systems meet the 30-day deadline? If backup copies require a longer period, please propose a maximum expiry period and explain how you would prevent access or reuse pending expiry and certify final deletion.

We can commit to deleting active copies and destroying geometry-bearing fixtures within 30 days. For backups, we propose keeping drawing material in an isolated workspace excluded from routine backups. If a specialist needs a disaster-recovery backup, we would list that exception in the attachment before sharing any material, with a maximum expiry of 90 days after the closeout trigger.

**Access and substitutions.** “The Access and Handling Schedule shall identify the specialist machining shop and accredited test laboratory by legal name and list the approved individuals, their tasks and the material each may receive. The shop may receive only the extracts needed to fabricate the approved fixtures. The laboratory may receive only the extracts needed for test setup and execution. The Testing House shall isolate those extracts, bind each recipient to the agreement’s confidentiality and use restrictions before disclosure, and remain responsible for compliance.”

“For a mid-job substitution, the Testing House shall submit the replacement’s qualifications, task and proposed access by email. The Design Owner shall respond within two business days and may withhold approval on reasonable grounds related to qualifications, confidentiality or information security. Access requires written approval. The Testing House shall revoke the outgoing specialist’s access and obtain confirmation of return or deletion before releasing material to the replacement, unless the parties approve a limited handover in writing.”

**Closeout and retention.** “The closeout period begins on written acceptance of the final report, 15 business days after delivery if the Design Owner has raised no specific objection in writing, or on earlier termination. Within 30 days after closeout begins, the Testing House shall securely erase all active copies, including specialist copies and derivative fixture files, and destroy physical fixtures that embody supplied geometry. It may retain test results and reports that neither disclose nor permit reconstruction of that geometry. It may retain calibration records for two years, with drawing material and geometry excluded.”

**Backups and verification.** “Any backup exception must be approved in the Access and Handling Schedule before disclosure. Listed backups shall be encrypted, segregated from active systems and accessible only to designated recovery administrators. They may be restored solely for disaster recovery into an isolated environment. After closeout, any restored drawing material shall be erased before the restored system is released for use. All listed backup copies shall expire no later than 90 days after closeout begins.”

“By day 30, the Testing House shall provide a signed destruction attestation identifying the materials by reference, deletion and destruction dates and methods, specialist confirmations, and any outstanding backup copies and their scheduled expiry dates. It shall certify final backup deletion within five business days after expiry. The Design Owner may have an independent verifier review the supporting records remotely, including deletion logs and specialist confirmations, without receiving CAD geometry or other customers’ information. If those records leave a specific issue unresolved, the parties may agree in advance on a focused, escorted inspection of the relevant area. This process replaces on-demand site access.”

We accept the proposed specialist access limits, substitution process, retention periods and backup deadlines. We can also accept a Testing House attestation at day 30, with independent remote review of the supporting records and a focused, escorted inspection only by prior agreement.

We propose four edits to close the remaining points.

1. **Named personnel.** “The Access and Handling Schedule shall name every individual authorized to access drawing material, including Testing House personnel, specialist personnel and any recovery administrator with access to that material. It shall identify each person’s task and permitted access. Before access, each individual and each recipient organization shall be bound in writing by confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. Additions require both parties’ written approval. Email approval is sufficient.”

2. **Copies, fixtures and reuse.** “The Testing House and approved recipients may make only the working copies reasonably needed for their scheduled tasks. All digital copies and extracts, including derivative fixture files, shall be encrypted in transit and at rest. Only the minimum geometry needed for an approved vibration-test fixture may be incorporated into its design or fabrication. No recipient may use the drawings, extracts, derivative files or geometry-bearing fixtures to develop or assist anyone in developing a competing product.”

3. **Report objections.** “If the Design Owner raises a specific written objection within the 15-business-day review period, a fresh 15-business-day review period begins on delivery of a revised final report addressing that objection. Written acceptance or earlier termination triggers closeout immediately.”

4. **Backup evidence.** “The Testing House shall retain the records supporting its final backup-deletion certificate, including evidence of actual expiry or deletion for each listed backup. Those records shall be available for the same independent remote review as the day-30 attestation.”

With those edits, we are ready to agree the wording. The parties can then complete and approve the Access and Handling Schedule before releasing any drawings.

We accept all four edits. The agreed wording limits use of drawing material to preparing, conducting and reporting the agreed actuator vibration tests. The day-30 attestation and any final backup-deletion certificate are subject to independent remote review. Any focused, escorted inspection requires prior agreement.

Before any drawings are released, both parties will approve the Access and Handling Schedule in writing. The Testing House will populate it with the machining shop and accredited laboratory, each authorized individual’s task and permitted material, and any backup exception requiring approval, including the named recovery administrators and maximum expiry. The schedule will also identify the calibration records retained for two years and confirm that they exclude drawing material and geometry. Mid-job substitutions will follow the agreed email approval and handover process.

Can you approve a written exception to the copying and disclosure restrictions for this review? We propose the following terms.

- Four festival programmers and one outside accessibility reviewer may view the unfinished cut through individual accounts. All five will agree in writing to keep the film confidential. Two of the five may each download one offline screener to an encrypted device. The others will stream it. No one may forward a screener or make clips.
- A programmer may give the selection board a short oral synopsis in a closed, confidential meeting. The board will hear the synopsis without receiving the screener or seeing footage.
- If selected, festival catalog staff may receive the synopsis in confidence and draft the entry before the announcement. We propose sending you the text for approval and publishing only after both your written approval and the official selection announcement. Permission to publish the approved text would apply even if the film itself has yet to premiere. Any stills or clips would require separate permission.
- When review ends, we will revoke viewing access, delete both offline copies, and remove the active screener from the platform. We need permission for the platform to retain its backup for 30 days after removal. The backup will be unavailable for review or publicity and deleted at the end of that period.

Please confirm which terms you can approve and identify any that need another rights holder’s consent. We’ll wait for written clearance before uploading the cut.

We can approve a written exception for review and catalog preparation on the terms below. Please send the five reviewers’ names, identify the two who need offline access, and confirm the festival and its platform can meet the withdrawal and backup terms. The draft’s blanket approval requirement would make it hard for depot staff to act on trial results. We propose replacing it with the following terms.

1. **Trial use.** Both parties may share measurements within the designated trial team as needed to run the trial, diagnose faults, and maintain the equipment. Raw failure traces and firmware parameters are restricted to designated trial team members who need them and are bound by the NDA.
2. **Contractor maintenance.** The depot operator may give its maintenance contractor the fault codes, affected equipment identifiers, and service instructions needed for assigned work, subject to equivalent confidentiality and use limits. Can the contractor complete its assigned work with those records and have the trial team investigate issues that require raw traces? If a specific task requires raw access, please identify the task and the fields needed so we can agree how to handle it.
3. **External reports.** Either party may circulate a proposed external report to the other for review at least 10 working days before release. The reviewer may flag confidential material, identifying details, or factual errors during that period. If the reviewer raises no objection by the deadline, the report may go out as submitted. The sensor maker may publish aggregate uptime across the three depots under this process, with route and depot identifiers and details that would reveal them removed. External reports must exclude raw failure traces and firmware parameters, subject to the safety exception below.
4. **Urgent safety.** Either party may disclose the minimum information needed to address an urgent safety risk to those in a position to act immediately. The disclosing party will notify the other as soon as practicable afterward, identifying what was shared and with whom.

We propose the following replacement terms for the three-depot trial.

1. **Trial use and repair.** We accept the proposed trial-team restrictions. For routine repairs, our contractor will receive the fault code, affected equipment ID and service instructions under equivalent confidentiality and use limits. If those records are insufficient, the trial team will review the raw trace and provide a diagnostic finding or repair instruction. If a technician needs trace data to complete the repair, our maintenance lead will identify the task and fields needed. Both trial leads must approve the specific extract and named recipient before release. The contractor will delete the extract when the repair is verified.

2. **Monthly board reporting.** Our trial lead may send the transit board a monthly report for internal use, without case-by-case clearance, and will send your trial lead the same report at the same time. The report may include fleetwide uptime, fault counts and repair summaries pooled across all three depots for the month. We will combine or omit small counts and distinctive events where staff could be identified. Reports will exclude depot/time pairs, route and equipment IDs, raw traces and firmware parameters. A board paper intended for a public agenda follows the publication process below.

3. **Publication.** Either party may submit the exact proposed release to the other party’s trial lead, including a sensor-maker report on pooled uptime. The same aggregation and exclusion rules apply. We accept your 10-working-day review period and approval by silence, measured from confirmed receipt. Either trial lead may object within that period by identifying the passage and the confidentiality, identification or factual issue. The publisher may omit the disputed material and release the undisputed remainder if it remains accurate. Revised disputed material requires written clearance from both leads before publication.

4. **Safety and required disclosures.** Either party may immediately share the information reasonably necessary to address an urgent safety risk with those able to act. Our safety lead may promptly notify the competent authorities of a serious incident, including when the immediate danger has passed, and provide necessary supporting detail. Neither prior notice nor approval is required for these disclosures. Each party may also make disclosures required by law within the applicable deadline. The disclosing party will tell the other as soon as practicable and legally permitted what it shared and with whom.

We can agree to the monthly board reporting and publication terms as drafted, including the sensor maker’s right to publish pooled uptime. The board may receive the monthly report for internal use without case-by-case clearance, and any version intended for a public agenda goes through the 10-working-day review from confirmed receipt.
